label: 0050 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 48 windows): 0049 with the Amur–southwest Japan block boundary along the whole 2016 Kumamoto rupture, reaching it at the Hinagu end along the south side of the Unzen graben, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0049 with cleaner block geometry at Kumamoto. In 0045–0049 the boundary between the Amur and southwest Japan (kuwana) blocks met the Kumamoto fault mesh at the Hinagu–Futagawa junction, so the 21 km Hinagu part of the mesh lay on no block boundary. Here the boundary follows the whole mesh, with two new segments on the northern Hinagu trace. The segment from Unzen now runs along the mapped faults on the south side of the Unzen graben and the north coast of the Uto Peninsula, then 24 km southeast across the eastern Uto Peninsula, where no fault is mapped, to the Hinagu end. The blocks' relative motion opens it at about 11 mm/yr, as it did the old connector. One site, 960696, moves to the Amur block. The base experiment has a new reference solve (block motion within 0.16 mm/yr of 0049's) and all 48 windows were rerun. Against 0049: window cross-validation −43, better in 31 of 48 windows (the loss is in the two short windows right after Tohoku); network fit unchanged (median ratio 0.9999) and Kyushu fit unchanged; residuals within 40 km of the new segments 7–15% lower in 1997–2003 and up to 0.17 mm/yr higher in some windows after 2016. Slow slip Mw is within 0.002 of 0049's and Kumamoto afterslip within 0.004 (Mw 6.78 at 1 yr, 6.85 at 2 yr).
